summary: Design role architectures, skills taxonomies, assessments, and HRIS workflows. Build an implementation roadmap through practical training. Enrol today.
lede: Designing and implementing skills-based organisations connects business priorities with deployable capability through a clear skills taxonomy, structured role architecture, and reliable workforce evidence. This course helps you identify critical skills, map work to roles, define proficiency levels, select assessment methods, and turn skills data into workforce actions. You will create practical outputs including a job architecture, taxonomy crosswalk, skills assessment matrix, HRIS and ERP data requirements, a workforce dashboard (Power BI or similar), and implementation roadmap. Using templates, sample workforce data, and case decisions, you will build a structured skills framework, an assessment approach, integration requirements, and an executive-ready action plan.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals responsible for connecting workforce capability with transformation, service delivery, and strategic planning. It suits experienced HR and organisational development practitioners as well as adjacent leaders who need to sponsor or govern a skills-based talent strategy.
prerequisites: You should have working experience in talent management, learning and development, workforce planning, organisational design, HR analytics, transformation, or HR technology. No programming is required. Familiarity with spreadsheets and basic workforce reporting will help, but the course introduces the core skills architecture concepts from the beginning. Bring a laptop if possible for dashboard and template exercises. Advanced AI-assisted skills inference and HRIS integration are taught at operational application level, not technical engineering level.
